      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle"><span class="qt2">Cholangiocarcinoma</span></content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>Your liver makes a digestive juice called bile. Your gallbladder stores it between meals. When you eat, your gallbladder pushes the bile into tubes called bile ducts. They carry the bile to your small intestine. The bile helps break down fat. It also helps the liver get rid of toxins and wastes.</p><p>Bile duct <span class="qt1">cancer</span> is rare. It can happen in the parts of the bile ducts that are outside or inside the liver. <span class="qt1">Cancer</span> of the bile duct outside of the liver is much more common. Risk factors include having inflammation of the bile duct, ulcerative colitis, and some liver diseases.</p><p>Symptoms can include:</p><ul><li>Jaundice</li><li>Itchy skin</li><li>Fever</li><li>Abdominal pain</li></ul><p>Tests to diagnose bile duct <span class="qt1">cancer</span> may include a physical exam, imaging tests of the liver and bile ducts, blood tests, and a biopsy.</p><p>Treatments include surgery, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy.</p><p>NIH: National <span class="qt1">Cancer</span> Institute</p></content>
